      <content name="altTitle"><span class="qt0">Thoracic</span> Injuries</content>
      <content name="FullSummary">What is the chest?<p>The chest is the part of your body between your neck and your abdomen (belly). The medical term for your chest is <span class="qt0">thorax</span>.</p><p>Your chest holds many important structures for breathing, digestion, blood circulation, and other important body functions. These structures include your:</p><ul><li>Ribs and breastbone</li><li>Esophagus, the tube between your mouth and stomach</li><li>Trachea, your windpipe</li><li>Bronchi, the tubes that carry air from your windpipe to your lungs</li><li>Lungs</li><li>Pleura, a thin layer of tissue that covers the lungs and lines the inside wall of the chest space</li><li>Heart and large blood vessels</li><li>Thymus, a gland that's part of your immune system</li><li>Nerves</li></ul>What are chest injuries and disorders?<p>Chest injuries and disorders are problems that affect any of the organs or structures located in your chest.</p><p>There are many types of chest injuries and disorders, for example:</p><ul><li>Broken ribs</li><li>Esophagus disorders</li><li>Swallowing disorders, also called dysphagia</li><li>Tracheal disorders</li><li>Bronchial disorders</li><li>Lung diseases and collapsed lung</li><li>Pleural disorders</li><li>Heart diseases</li><li>Mediastinal diseases, which are tumors, inflammation, and other problems with the structures in the mediastinum, which is the space between your lungs, breastbone, and spine</li><li><span class="qt0">Thoracic</span> aortic aneurysm</li><li><span class="qt0">Thoracic</span> outlet syndrome</li></ul><p>Chest injuries may happen from the force of car accidents, falls, or sports injuries. Or the chest may be pierced by a bullet or sharp object. Because your chest holds so many important structures, certain chest injuries may be life-threatening.</p>How are chest injuries and disorders diagnosed?<p>Diagnosis of chest injuries or disorders depends on the type of symptoms you're having and whether you've had a chest injury. Injuries are usually obvious, but in most cases, you'll need tests to know how serious an injury is.</p><p>There are many types of tests for diagnosing different types of chest injuries and disorders, for example:</p><ul><li>Diagnostic imaging tests</li><li>Heart tests</li><li>Lung function tests</li><li>Bronchoscopy</li><li>Pleural fluid analysis</li><li>Dysphagia tests</li><li>Biopsy</li></ul><p>Treatments will depend on the type of chest injury or disorder you have.</p></content>
